topSignals.title: Germany's Netzpaket: Bundesrat files a formal critical opinion revealing a concrete 18-20% uncompensated-curtailment risk for behind-the-meter generation — the Oct 16 target vote date passed with no plenary vote.
topSignals.text: A Bundestag "hib" release (Oct 2, Drucksache 21/7866, Bundesrat opinion published as Unterrichtung 21/8299) shows the Bundesrat arguing the draft contains no real grid-expansion acceleration and instead slows renewables buildout — objecting specifically to the grid-expansion requirements, priority rules, and the Redispatch-Vorbehalt clause. In capacity-constrained grid areas, the draft would let operators get a connection only if they accept no compensation for up to 18-20% of annual output lost to network-related curtailment — the first time this monitor has found a quantified figure for the clause most relevant to SOFC behind-the-meter/islanded deployment in Germany. The federal government's Gegenäußerung rejects the Länder's proposals outright. Despite this monitor's Oct 5 "final vote targeted around Oct 16" marker, no plenary vote outcome was found as of this check — the bill remains in committee/Bundesrat back-and-forth. Bundestag hib 767/2026 | Tagesspiegel Background — "Mehr Kritik als Zustimmung für Netzpaket"
